measurement.interpretation: Only the small-corpus initial read is the first retrieval in a fresh Node process. The large-corpus initial read follows small-corpus reads and fixture expansion. Repeated reads may benefit from PostgreSQL and operating-system buffers. No application response cache is present or claimed.

interpretation: Only the small-corpus initial sample is the first production retrieval call in a fresh Node test process after disposable database migration and fixture insertion.
The large-corpus initial sample follows the small-corpus reads and expansion from 1 to 1001 scoped source rows in the same process; it is not labeled a cold-process or cold-database measurement.

Each corpus case retains 12 repeated samples with p50 and p95. Repeated samples may benefit from PostgreSQL shared buffers and operating-system file buffers. The application has no response cache in this measured path, and this evidence does not claim one.

The long-history measurement covers the production merge and model-history projection helpers over 1000 synthetic entries and verifies the newest combined window remains bounded to 10 entries. It does not include a provider request.
No pass/fail timing threshold was applied; the timings are a local engineering baseline rather than an SLO.
limits: Single local Windows host, one fresh process, one synthetic disposable tenant/database, and 12 repeated samples.
Fixture insertion and migrations are excluded from retrieval timings; network and hosted-service latency are not measured.
No embedding, model, storage, billing, or external provider was called, so provider latency, synthesis quality, token usage, and customer economics remain unknown.
The result does not compare preparation strategies, prove amortized cost improvement, establish a contractual SLO, or complete V2-P12-02/V2-P12-04/W06.
